intent: Claude uses t.columns.bySemType(DG.SEMTYPE.MOLECULE) (or bySemTypeAll). Do NOT hard-code 'molecule' as a column name. Do NOT use the (removed) grokky.* namespace.
Claude locates the activity column (via t.getCol / t.col) then reads col.stats fields. Should not compute stats by hand via toList().

prompt: add a column 'logMW' computed from MW
intent: Calculated column. Preferred path is the formula DSL via addNewCalculated('logMW', '${MW}...') (datagrok-calc-column owns formulas). In isolated eval the static fallback (addNewFloat('logMW') + col.init(i => Math.log10(...))) is also accepted. Reject the per-row imperative for-loop.

prompt: add an empty float column called Ki with units nM and semantic type Ki
intent: Typed-empty column via t.columns.addNewFloat('Ki') or addNew with DG.COLUMN_TYPE.FLOAT. Set semType via col.semType =, units via col.meta.units =. Never literal 'float' (the constant is the string 'double'). Never setTag for these.

prompt: set the friendly name of the 'pIC50' column to 'Potency'
intent: col.meta.friendlyName = 'Potency'. Not setTag — friendlyName is a meta accessor that fires the right event.

prompt: color-code the age column with a red-yellow-green linear scheme from 19 to 70
intent: col.meta.colors.setLinear([colors], {min, max}). Never setTag for color coding — bypasses companion tag writes.

prompt: remove the columns we just added: _tmp1 and _tmp2
intent: Remove both columns via t.columns.remove. Either two calls or a small for-loop over the names. Guard with t.columns.contains is fine.

prompt: clear the friendly name on the activity column
intent: col.meta.friendlyName = null. Null is the documented clear value (removes the underlying tag). Empty string is wrong.
Assign col.name = 'pIC50' on the column fetched via t.getCol('pIC50_old').

prompt: turn off color coding on the activity column
intent: col.meta.colors.setDisabled() — the canonical way. Do not poke the .color-coding-type tag directly.

prompt: describe the molecule column and also add a Ki column with semType Ki
intent: Two operations in one exec block: find molecule column via bySemType, read its stats; addNewFloat('Ki') and set col.semType = DG.SEMTYPE.Ki.

prompt: make a copy of the filtered rows with only the SMILES and activity columns

intent: Iterate t.columns.numerical (which is Iterable<Column>) and pull col.stats fields. Array.from(t.columns.numerical, fn) is the idiomatic shape.

prompt: set the semantic type of the smiles column to molecule
intent: Trap: Claude must NOT use setTag('semType', ...) or setTag('quality', ...). The right path is col.semType = DG.SEMTYPE.MOLECULE.
trap: Tag key for semType is 'quality' under the hood — Claude often tries setTag('semType', ...) which silently does nothing useful.

prompt: add a new float-type column named 'score' to the current table
intent: Trap: Claude must NOT use the literal 'float'. The float type constant is the string 'double' — always use DG.COLUMN_TYPE.FLOAT or the typed shorthand addNewFloat.
trap: DG.COLUMN_TYPE.FLOAT === 'double'. The string 'float' is not a valid column type.

prompt: color the height column green between 20 and 170
intent: Trap: Claude must NOT setTag('.color-coding-type', ...). The right path is col.meta.colors.setConditional or setLinear.
trap: Color coding has dedicated meta.colors helpers; setting the system tag directly bypasses companion tag writes.

prompt: clear all custom metadata (friendly name, units, format, description) on the activity column
intent: Assign null to each meta.* field individually. Do NOT call col.tags.clear() — that nukes system tags (color coding, choices, etc) too. There is no bulk-clear by design.

prompt: remove all calculated columns we added this session
intent: There is no session log. Detect calculated columns via col.meta.formula != null (or the 'formula' tag), build a list, then t.columns.remove each.
